requirements_summary: Workload: multi-tenant chat/agent orchestration; long-running streaming sessions with tool calls (calendar, ticket creation, internal search).
Latency targets: 95th <= 250-350ms for token streaming in core flows; p99 tails acceptable up to 700ms but want mitigation strategies.
Throughput: spikes to 120 concurrent sessions / region during peak; bursty tenant traffic expected (startup customers).
Rate-limiting: strict per-tenant quotas expected; want soft caps + graceful backpressure (not hard 429s) and token-level billing transparency.
Availability/DR: multi-region fallback (NA primary, EU secondary) and automatic model fallback if capacity constrained.
Security/compliance: SSO/SAML, audit logs retained 1 year, KMS for key management, contract-level data residency for EU enterprise customers.
Model preferences: flexible to open models but want Redwood recommendations for quantized variants; tool-calling and structured output important.
Observability: per-tenant latency/cost dashboards; request traces for streaming sessions and KV cache hit metrics.
notes: AE notes: Good technical understanding; CTO (Martin Cho) very concerned about p95/p99 streaming stability — quoted: 'if streaming jitters, customer experience collapses',
Call paraphrase: Wants 'noisy neighbor' isolation per tenant and a way to throttle tiers; asked about per-route token budgets and burst windows.

POC plan: 2-week hosted API POC simulating 10 tenants with mixed SLAs; test cases: steady-state chat, concurrent tool-calls, prefix caching effectiveness, simultaneous streaming to multiple browser tabs.
Pricing sensitivity: willing to commit to Dedicated once unit economics prove out; short-term interest in hosted to validate UX and latency; ask for commitment tier pricing and overage mechanics.
Red flags: legal asked for data flow diagram (we provided); security wants SOC2 docs + crisp audit log retention story.
